_comment: Reference facts for every document in heldout/nhtsa/data/complaints/, written by Claude Opus 5.5 on 2026-09-24 (R51)
from the narratives alone, before any pipeline output for this dataset existed (no run had been made on it).
Not a human gold standard. Goal of the benchmark, given to every run with --goal: 'vehicle safety root cause
analysis: from a problem an owner reports, reach the component that fails and the recall that covers it'.
Automatic arm: no schema is pinned, so the predicates are Claude's own vocabulary, chosen before any proposal:
HAS_PROBLEM (a component, or the vehicle when no component is named, to a problem it shows), CAUSES (a problem,
or a component whose failure the text names, to a problem or event the text says it leads to), PART_OF (every
component that is the subject of a problem or a cause, once per document, to the document's vehicle),
COVERED_BY_RECALL (a component to a recall the text names). R52 maps each of them to one predicate of the
proposed schema, or marks it not expressible; the mapping is listed in REFACTOR_PLAN R52 and this file's R51
version stays in git.
Rules: the subject is the component the text names as producing the problem, also when it is named in a
when-clause (the Civic's cruise control and lane keeping assist, engaged together), else the vehicle by its
document name; one event told twice in a complaint, or one claim made by two complaints of a document, is one
triple. Names leave out when/if clauses and frequency words, unless the clause is what is wrong: then the name
says so ('premature auto-shutoff', the one name not copied from the text). A sentence listing several problems
gives one triple per item; a general problem and its specific forms are all kept when all are stated.
Reviewed by the user on 2026-09-24, before any run (R51 part 2, not a gold correction: no output existed):
the Civic cruise control and lane keeping assist became the subjects of that complaint's problems, the second
windshield crack and the Rogue's vehicle-level copy of its camera braking were removed as repeats, the
placeholder 'part failure' was replaced by the piston clip ring as the cause, 'auto-shutoff' says what is
wrong. Not facts: dealer visits, repairs
made, mileage, dates, opinions about the maker, explanations the text reports as someone else's claim, vague
problem words ('having issues'), hypothetical outcomes ('could cause an accident'), injuries from a crash the
text does not blame on a problem. One triple per distinct claim per document; `evidence` is a verbatim quote.
er_pairs: both names occur as whole words in the corpus; for vehicles `same` means the same vehicle, for every
other type the same kind of thing. questions: `expected` holds the vehicles' `model` values or recall campaign
numbers from data/; the Cypher is written in R52 against the proposed plan and schema (until then 'MATCH' only).
R52 (2026-09-24, Claude Opus 5.5): the automatic arm's plan and text schema were proposed by heldout run
(tests/gold/heldout_nhtsa_plan.json, heldout_nhtsa_text_schema.json) and the predicates mapped to that schema
before any extraction output existed; every triple keeps its R51 labels in `labelled_as`. Mapping, done by a
fixed rule: component HAS_PROBLEM problem -> problem OCCURS_IN_COMPONENT component (same claim, inverted);
vehicle HAS_PROBLEM problem -> 'Complaint <ODI number>' REPORTS_PROBLEM problem (the schema has no
vehicle-problem relation; the claim moves to the complaint whose section holds the evidence); PART_OF ->
PART_OF_VEHICLE (derived in code); COVERED_BY_RECALL -> the complaint MENTIONS_RECALL the recall; CAUSES is
not expressible in the schema and stays as it was: those 5 triples can only be missed (a loss the schema causes).
Question Cypher written in R52 against the proposed labels (Vehicle.model, Recall.NHTSACampaignNumber, entity
types Problem / Component / Recall); names and aliases are read as for the furniture questions.

questions.question: Which recall campaigns of the 2015 Ford Escape concern its automatic transmission? (domain graph only)
questions.cypher: MATCH (r:Recall)-[:AFFECTS_VEHICLE]->(:Vehicle {model: 'ESCAPE'}) WHERE r.Component CONTAINS 'AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION' RETURN DISTINCT r.NHTSACampaignNumber

questions.question: Which vehicles do owners report braking on its own or suddenly?
questions.cypher: MATCH (c:Chunk)-[:MENTIONS]->(p:Entity {type: 'Problem'}) WHERE any(n IN [p.name] + coalesce(p.aliases, []) WHERE toLower(n) CONTAINS 'brak' AND (toLower(n) CONTAINS 'sudden' OR toLower(n) CONTAINS 'its own' OR toLower(n) CONTAINS 'activat')) MATCH (c)-[:PART_OF]->(:Document)-[:ABOUT]->(v:Vehicle) RETURN DISTINCT v.model

questions.question: Which vehicles do owners report with a cracked windshield?
questions.cypher: MATCH (c:Chunk)-[:MENTIONS]->(p:Entity {type: 'Problem'}) WHERE any(n IN [p.name] + coalesce(p.aliases, []) WHERE toLower(n) CONTAINS 'crack') AND (any(n IN [p.name] + coalesce(p.aliases, []) WHERE toLower(n) CONTAINS 'windshield') OR EXISTS { MATCH (p)-[:OCCURS_IN_COMPONENT]->(w:Entity) WHERE any(n IN [w.name] + coalesce(w.aliases, []) WHERE toLower(n) CONTAINS 'windshield') }) MATCH (c)-[:PART_OF]->(:Document)-[:ABOUT]->(v:Vehicle) RETURN DISTINCT v.model

questions.question: Which vehicles do owners report with air bags that failed to deploy?
questions.cypher: MATCH (c:Chunk)-[:MENTIONS]->(p:Entity {type: 'Problem'}) WHERE any(n IN [p.name] + coalesce(p.aliases, []) WHERE toLower(n) CONTAINS 'deploy') MATCH (c)-[:PART_OF]->(:Document)-[:ABOUT]->(v:Vehicle) RETURN DISTINCT v.model

questions.question: Which engine recall campaign belongs to the vehicle whose owners report a piston ring recall?
questions.cypher: MATCH (c:Chunk)-[:MENTIONS]->(e:Entity) WHERE e.type IN ['Recall', 'Component'] AND any(n IN [e.name] + coalesce(e.aliases, []) WHERE toLower(n) CONTAINS 'piston') MATCH (c)-[:PART_OF]->(:Document)-[:ABOUT]->(:Vehicle)<-[:AFFECTS_VEHICLE]-(r:Recall) WHERE r.Component STARTS WITH 'ENGINE' RETURN DISTINCT r.NHTSACampaignNumber
